adherence.reason: The narrative is structured as a mystery, with a suspicious body, planted clues, old case-file parallels, and an unknown voice.
Elara is identified as a young detective, the only officer on duty for the county, and the ending explicitly calls this her first solo case.
The text explicitly says her anxiety drove her to memorize every unsolved case file in the precinct archive.
The action occurs on the third day of a severe blizzard that has cut Oakhaven off by road, power, and cell service.
The active narrative is consistently told in present tense; past and past-perfect forms are confined to prior events and quoted case history.
Mr. Higgins is the missing shopkeeper, and Elara reports that his store was found locked from the outside the previous week.

Elara recognizes that the disappearance may reuse a memorized case-file template as a test, but the story repeatedly hedges between Higgins, an imitator, and a killer and never clearly reveals that Higgins staged it himself.
